dimensions.gloss: How much of the output or task the AI produced or performed, expressed as an ordered level, band, or category.
variants: five distinct levels of genai integration in assessment
five progressive levels of genai proficiency

dimensions.gloss: Which action the human took on an AI-produced output, such as accepting, editing, or rejecting it.
The literal text or sample wording used to disclose AI or contribution, as opposed to whether or where it appears.
Whether a specific commercial fact (the brand, the product, or receipt of compensation) was mentioned in an advertising disclosure.
Whether a conflict-of-interest or financial-relationship disclosure was made and what it reported.
dimensions.note: 'disclosures' is a bare checklist subitem (12a) paired in its source with a funding subitem (12b); grouped here with financial COI status rather than funding source, since both concern reporting of interests/relationships rather than which funder paid.

dimensions.gloss: Whether and which funding source (e.g. public, pharmaceutical, other company) is declared as supporting the work.
Whether a policy explicitly discourages, prohibits, or assigns human responsibility for AI-generated content, as a set of yes/no policy-content flags.
variants: discourage ai usage for content generation, such as text, figure, images
explicit prohibition of ai tools as authors
emphasis on responsibility for human authors on ai generated content

dimensions.gloss: Which stakeholder group (authors vs. journals/editorial teams) a set of AI-use recommendations is addressed to.
What kinds of activity or role (drafting, conception, data curation, accountability, etc.) qualify a contributor for authorship or a named role.
variants: drafted the first version of the paper or revised it critically for important intellectual content
documentation of individual contributions (qualitative and quantitative)
gai use should be mapped using the contributor roles taxonomy
dimensions.note: 'do not meet authorship criteria' and 'execution' are close calls: the former names the negative case of this same axis, the latter is a role label from an activity taxonomy structurally parallel to the CRediT-style roles here.

dimensions.gloss: Where within the manuscript (acknowledgements, cover letter, methods, a new section, or a dedicated statement) AI use must be reported.
variants: gai use reported in a new section of the manuscript
gai use reported in acknowledgements section
gai use reported in cover letter
gai use reported in materials and methods section
gai use should be reported in a gait statement
dimensions.note: The GAIT-statement item is a close call: it mandates a dedicated named statement rather than an existing section, but shares the same underlying question of where disclosure is placed.

dimensions.gloss: A meta-level enumeration of which policy components (prohibition, disclosure requirement, detection-tool reference, etc.) an AI-use policy scheme covers.
Whether a data object meets FAIR 'Findable' sub-criteria: a global unique identifier, rich metadata, metadata carrying the identifier, and registration in a searchable resource.
variants: f4. registered in a searchable resource

dimensions.gloss: Whether/how well a repository supports or requires documentation that aids proper reuse of deposited data.
Whether a repository accepts metadata applicable to a specific community's (dkNET) discipline-specific needs.
Whether a repository's metadata uses formal, shared vocabularies that follow FAIR knowledge-representation principles.
The organizing structure (themes, or graduated levels of action) of one FAIR-data reporting framework, as a meta-description rather than a single content axis.
dimensions.note: Close call: both are meta-descriptions of one framework's internal structure (its themes vs. its graduated levels) rather than a disclosure content axis in their own right; grouped together as the same kind of structural label.

dimensions.gloss: Whether and how an output, claim, or use can be traced back to the evidence, source, or factors it is based on.
What happens, and who is notified, when a failure, risk increase, or warning sign occurs during AI-assisted use.
The point at which a case or item enters or exits a governed process or generation stance.
dimensions.note: Close call: quotes for both are cryptic fragments from the same source; paired on the shared entry/exit framing.

dimensions.gloss: Whether errors, subgroup performance gaps, or accuracy metrics of an AI system are logged and reported.
High-level stated principles (accountability, confidentiality, equity, adaptive governance) that a scheme asserts should guide AI use in research.

For a given category of health-technology-assessment content (economic model, efficacy/safety, epidemiology, cost, health gain, patient numbers), whether publishing it is mandatory, recommended, or not required.
variants: economic modelling methodology (model type, time horizon, discount rate, etc.)
efficacy and safety of the new technology
epidemiology of the target indication (incidence, prevalence)
estimated current resource use and treatment costs of patients
estimated patient numbers and market share of new technology in next 3–5 years
estimated resource use and treatment costs of patients with the new technology

dimensions.gloss: Whether the person relying on AI-assisted output can explain, defend, or audit it, and whether the output itself is a transparent (non-black-box) artifact.
The regulatory mode or tier of a disclosure obligation, from routine notice to specific authorization, or declarative vs. infrastructural rendering.
variants: focus of the duty to inform
dimensions.note: Close call: one is a conceptual framework's rendering-condition typology, the other a regulatory duty-to-inform tier list; grouped as both classify the mode/intensity of a legal disclosure obligation.

dimensions.gloss: The stylistic register of a disclosure's text: its emotional tone, level of explicit detail, and neutral vs. warning-like framing.
Whether and how consequences (sanctions, retraction, reporting) for non-compliance with a disclosure policy are specified.
Whether algorithmic bias, subgroup disparity, or fairness is addressed as a disclosed consideration.
Whether the work underwent formal ethical review or approval (e.g. IRB) as a disclosed research-activity domain.
Whether a dual/independent check or a fact-and-reference check was carried out and recorded on AI-assisted content.
Technical specifics of the AI system used (tool, version, algorithm, input-data procedure) that a scheme requires be reported.
variants: elements that require detailed and specific reporting

dimensions.gloss: What role or purpose the AI tool served in the work, including the prompts/input and the reasoning for using it.
variants: gai tool's role in the study

dimensions.gloss: Whether and how collaboration between students and faculty is discussed/disclosed.
The rated complexity/severity of the disease context a case involves.
Whether a regulatory document distinguishes the role of an AI verifier from that of the underlying tool provider.
The type of divergence (semantic, numerical, classification, temporal, version, authority) between two claims being compared.
The type of document (bill passed, bill rejected, web article, etc.) sampled in a policy/legal corpus.
The legal elements (control over the generative process, verifiable creative input, identifiable expressive intent) used to decide authorship of an AI-generated work.
variants: effective control over the generative process

dimensions.gloss: A dual construct rating whether an AI use fits the research task (effectiveness) and aligns with institutional/professional norms (legitimacy).
A meta-list naming the elements (transparency, responsibility, understanding, supervision, tiered use) that make up one policy scheme.
The denominator-defining eligibility criteria (inclusion/exclusion, encounter type) for patients under an AI clinical-decision-support protocol.
Whether an AI component was retained as a heavyweight runtime dependency or distilled away for resource/energy efficiency.
Whether an English translation of the disclosure/document is required.
The categories of entity (artefacts, claims, sources, transcripts, prompts) a provenance scheme tracks.
Separation of the task-bound control object from the evidence object within a governance architecture.
Whether an AI tool is credited with reducing a language barrier as an equity-related function.
The essential properties (security, compliance, storage, unforgeability, overhead, revocability) a data-provenance system should satisfy.
A broad thematic stance on ethical AI use, e.g. that outright prohibition is not a sustainable policy response.
A composite indicator category bundling bias/fairness flags, privacy notes, and risk indicators together.
A bare numbered checklist item flagging that ethical considerations were addressed, without further specification.

dimensions.canonical_label: Ethical implications of AI in the university setting
dimensions.gloss: A thematic bucket of sub-concerns (research integrity, IP, funder guidelines) about AI use in a university context.
variants: ethical implications of ai use in the university setting

dimensions.gloss: One summary category, alongside permitted/prohibited uses and disclosure/verification requirements, covering what ethical safeguards a scheme specifies.
Whether safety checklists or red-teaming were applied to AI-generated prompts/outputs before deployment.
Which named instrument (GQS, mDISCERN, JAMA benchmark, ICC, etc.) was used to evaluate AI-generated content quality.
A controlled classification scheme for evidence that enables interpretation without redefining the underlying object.
The format/category of a structured acknowledgment statement, e.g. named individual, collective, or confidential support role.
Whether an applicable exit/opt-out procedure was documented.
A pre-specified profile of what evidence is expected, preventing a system from self-creating its own governed evidentiary basis.
The research domain or use-case (microbiology, plant science, graphical abstracts, etc.) in which an AI tool was applied.
A framework governing how expert testimony is treated, referenced without further detail in the source.
A thematic bucket of considerations external to the institution, e.g. alignment with law, individual responsibility, potential harm.
A forensic-analysis layer (e.g. spectral/phase anomalies, prosody continuity) used to detect synthetic media.
A named framework's list of guardrail principles (human first, no hidden substitution, AI as challenger, etc.) for faculty overseeing AI-assisted student work.
The legal fair-use factors (purpose/character, nature of training data, amount used, market impact) applied to AI training data.
How a system's technical realism (fidelity) interacts with whether it carries persistent, unambiguous disclosure.
Separation of a data value from its origin and review disposition.
The final status code (required, recommended, conditional, contextual, excluded) assigned to a checklist item.
The first and current release date recorded as software/dataset metadata.
The named layers (governance/public, infrastructure, institution/platform, evaluation, user labor) of one governance framework.
A meta-list of the elements (declaration, navigation, documentation account, process documentation, development records) that operationalize meaningful human control through transparency.
A qualitative typology of the mode of cognitive relationship between a person and AI, from lone to systemic.
variants: five-level taxonomy of human cognitive agency

dimensions.gloss: A named operation category (e.g. forwarding standardized, low-impact text) within a workplace AI-task typology.
A meta-framework organizing provenance questions around source, identity, context, and circulation.
The type of learning outcome (assisted performance, independent acquisition, AI-integrated performance, transfer) resulting from AI-assisted tasks.
A meta-list of four themes of deceptive or harmful AI-related disclosure practice in advertising.
A tiered typology of tasks used to organize AI-use rubrics.
The rhetorical/functional role (background, method, finding, limitation) tagged onto a unit of synthesized content.
What purpose a software mention in text serves: enabling identification, crediting contributors, or aiding reuse.
Whether GenAI use is characterized as enhancing or replacing the human role.
The parallel fronts (theoretical, empirical, technical) along which a research agenda on distributed AI/human agency is organized.
